title: LeBron Records First Triple-Double as a 76er and Durant Joins the 33,000-Point Club as the NBA Cup Rolls On — Spurs' 11-Game Win Streak Snapped in Portland
excerpt: LeBron James posted his first triple-double in a Philadelphia uniform as the 76ers beat Miami 111-104, Kevin Durant became the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 career points in Houston's 116-104 win over Phoenix, and Portland ended San Antonio's 11-game winning streak 116-111.
content:
PHILADELPHIA — LeBron James recorded his first triple-double as a 76er on Wednesday night, finishing with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds as Philadelphia beat the Miami Heat 111-104 in Emirates NBA Cup group play.

It was James' best game since joining Philadelphia, and after the win he praised Erik Spoelstra — his coach during Miami's championship seasons — calling him the best coach he had in Miami.

In Houston, Kevin Durant reached 33,000 career points as the Rockets beat the Phoenix Suns 116-104. Durant became just the fifth player in NBA history to reach the mark, joining James, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant.

The game ended in a confrontation between Durant and his former team. Suns forward Dillon Brooks was ejected after a chest-to-chest standoff with Durant near half court; it was Brooks' second technical foul of the night, an automatic ejection, after he had already been whistled for one at the 4:32 mark of the fourth quarter. The win also eliminated Phoenix from Cup contention.

In Portland, the Trail Blazers ended the San Antonio Spurs' 11-game winning streak with a 116-111 win, despite 44 points and 16 rebounds from Victor Wembanyama. Deni Avdija scored 33 points for Portland and hit a crucial late three-pointer after the game was tied at 109. Wembanyama drew a sixth foul on Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan, who fouled out defending the Spurs star and was caught on camera calling him 'soft' — then accused him of flopping from the sideline. The Spurs' streak had reached 11 with their 123-85 rout of Golden State on Nov. 13.

Elsewhere in Cup play on Wednesday, the Dallas Mavericks beat the Denver Nuggets 120-101 behind 24 points and 12 assists from Cooper Flagg, the Boston Celtics beat the Washington Wizards 131-116 as Jayson Tatum scored 41, and the Chicago Bulls held off the Charlotte Hornets 107-105 behind 24 points from Matas Buzelis.

Through Thursday, the Los Angeles Lakers lead the Western Conference at 15-3, with the Spurs right behind at 15-4. The 76ers lead the East at 15-4, followed by the Boston Celtics and New York Knicks at 12-6. Friday night brings a heavyweight matchup as the Spurs host the Lakers at Frost Bank Center, the Knicks host the Heat at Madison Square Garden, and the 76ers visit the Indiana Pacers.

Sources: Essentially Sports, Nov. 26, 2026; The Orbit Post, Nov. 26, 2026; Sportradar, Nov. 27, 2026; Hoopster, Nov. 27, 2026.
